perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- He is an accountant at a small community center and works with Martha Moua as a colleague, mainly in work-related interactions.
- While reviewing financial reports, he noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns. He became suspicious and anxious, initially believing Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- He asked Martha to discuss the recent financial report and pointed out the healthcare expense discrepancy. He heard Martha say there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct errors.
- After reviewing the matter with Martha, Mason came to believe the discrepancies were a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved but embarrassed about his initial suspicion.
- He thanked Martha for clarifying the numbers and apologized for suspecting her. He heard Martha say errors happen, she understood he was being thorough, and they should double-check entries next time.
- Mason then believed Martha was competent, while the recurring clerical errors showed him the financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha.
- He told Martha the issue was not her management but the current system. He proposed a new, more robust financial system, said he would draft a proposal, and asked for her input. He heard Martha agree and offer to help address the gaps.
- Mason drafted the proposal. He hoped it would benefit operations but was uncertain whether management would approve and implement it.
- He told Martha he had finished the draft. He heard Martha call it solid, encourage him to present it confidently, and agree to help gather data. He planned to prepare a detailed presentation.
- Mason presented the proposal to management. He felt the presentation went well, was satisfied with his effort, but was physically and mentally exhausted. He believed he had done everything he could and that the decision was now up to management.
- He told Martha this. He heard Martha praise his work, suggest he take time off, and offer help while he was away. He planned to take a few days off to recharge, reflect, and hope for good news.
